title: A planar triangular Dy3 + Dy3 single-molecule magnet with a toroidal magnetic moment

synthesis.procedure: 4,6-Dihydrazinopyrimidine (0.1 mmol) was dissolved in methanol/acetonitrile (1:2, 15 mL), and o-vanillin (0.2 mmol) was added. The mixture was stirred for 5 min, then KOH (0.2 mmol) and DyBr3·6H2O (0.2 mmol) were added successively. The mixture was stirred at room temperature for 3 h and left for slow solvent evaporation. Yellow crystals of Dy6[Br] formed after about one week. H2L is the in situ Schiff-base ligand from 4,6-dihydrazinopyrimidine and o-vanillin. The main text only states that reaction of H2L with DyBr3·6H2O followed by KOH gave yellow crystals over about one week, without quantities.
synthesis.time: stirred 3 h; crystals after about one week
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction followed by slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: resultant solution left unperturbed for slow evaporation; yellow single crystals
synthesis.yield: 25 mg (24.8%, based on the metal salt)

properties.summary: Dy6[Br] is a zero-field SMM with two relaxation processes and a toroidal magnetic moment in the ground state. χMT falls from 83.9 cm3 mol−1 K at room temperature to 10.36 cm3 mol−1 K at 2 K. The fast-relaxation barrier is 98 K (stated as 97.7 K in the conclusion), comparable to the Dy6–SCN and Dy6–NO3 analogues, while axial water ligands reorient the Dy easy axes into a toroidal arrangement.
